components.label: app
responsibilities: Composition root: wire the HTTP repository into the order screen and start the app.
forbidden_responsibilities: Order rules, persistence details and widget layout.

requires.rationale: The composition root starts the order screen.
The composition root chooses the repository implementation the screen is given.

components.label: presentation
responsibilities: Pages and widgets that show orders.
forbidden_responsibilities: HTTP, JSON and deciding what an order is.

requires.rationale: Widgets render the domain's orders and load them through its repository port.

components.label: domain
responsibilities: Order entities and the repository port every implementation fulfils.
forbidden_responsibilities: Widgets, platform I/O and any transport.

components.label: data
responsibilities: Load and save orders over HTTP.

requires.rationale: The HTTP repository implements the domain's port and builds its entities.

rules.rationale: A cross-component import nobody asked for is an accident, so each component names what it needs and absence refuses the rest.
Components stay layered so each one can be reviewed and replaced in dependency order.
A library without one owning component escapes every boundary rule.
lib/ holds only the entry point and the three declared layers.
Components meet only at their declared libraries and names, so reaching past a facade requires a visible contract change.
The two platform clients are alternatives of one conditional import, so neither may depend on the other.
The domain runs unchanged in a browser build, which has no dart:io.
A package no rule names is a package nobody chose; the dart: core libraries are the standard library and need no rule.
Only the entry point and the widgets know Flutter, so order rules stay testable without a widget tree.
Only the data layer speaks HTTP; everything else sees the repository port.
